new_scholarship.description: The Charlie Perkins Scholarship Trust funds Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians to undertake full-time postgraduate study at the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge. Each award covers up to three years of full university and college fees, travel costs and an annual stipend of GBP 20,810 for 2025-2026. Applications open in early October and close at the end of January each year, so the window is open now.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as such and be accepted by their community, supply written confirmation of Indigenous identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council, and be applying for or enrolled in a full-time postgraduate course at Oxford or Cambridge.

new_scholarship.description: The New Zealand Refugee Health Scholarship pays health-related study costs for former refugees and their children already living in New Zealand, and is administered through Universities New Zealand. Each recipient receives up to NZD 25,000 for one academic year, being NZD 5,000 toward course costs plus a NZD 20,000 living stipend. The 2027 intake closed on 1 October 2026 and the programme runs annually.

Immigration New Zealand notes the programme particularly values scholars with cultural knowledge and indigenous language skills.

rejected.candidate: Medical Research Scholarship (New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes, NZFWI)
rejected.reason: Not open to applicants and not a study award. The Federation's own page states 'Medical Research Scholarship nominations come from the members', with members using a nomination form for the National Executive Council to consider at its meeting in February, and says 'Applications will be called for in December 2027' - a date more than 14 months away, outside the roughly 10-month window the brief allows, and not an application window at all. It is also a research grant to a project or researcher rather than funding a student's study.

rejected.candidate: Canterbury Women's Legal Association scholarships (Top Non-Honours Female Law Student, Lady Dorothy Thompson Scholarships)
rejected.reason: No route to apply. The CWLA's own page states the Top Non-Honours Female Law Student award is 'chosen by way of recommendation by the Law School' with 'No application is required', and the Lady Dorothy Thompson Scholarships go to the top two women at the Institute of Professional Legal Studies, presented at the association's AGM with no application route published. The women's scholarships listed on that page under other organisations (Yvonne A M Smith, Sir William Hartley, Graduate Women Canterbury Branch) are all University of Canterbury awards, so they belong to the university scholarship cell, not this one.

An aggregator, not an awarding body. The page is a searchable directory of scholarships offered by Australian universities and one private provider, and REA's own words are that it 'has played a role in advocating for these scholarships'. It funds nothing itself, so it fails the test of a body that awards the money. I used it only as a discovery lead to the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship, which I verified on ILSC's own site instead.
